comparison: Perfect agreement on AG fibroblast identification and characterization (C2, C28-C35). Both evaluations find the evidence solid and well-supported, with reviewers explicitly affirming this as a novel and distinct subpopulation.

Complete agreement on AG fibroblast localization (C3, C42, C43). Both evaluations support the anatomical positioning data without concerns, though OpenEval notes the immune surveillance inference is reasonable while peer review implicitly accepts it.

Both address AG fibroblast activation in early periodontitis. OpenEval covers C4, C5, C36, C37, C39, C40, C41 while peer review covers C4, C5, C36, C37, C39, C40, C48-C57. Both find evidence supported, though OpenEval notes C41 (initiating inflammation) is somewhat speculative. Peer review accepts findings from both ligature and MTA models together.

OpenEval evaluates MTA model findings (C48-C58) as supported with C58 being speculative. Peer review groups these claims with ligature model data and finds them supported, noting qualification relates to mechanistic depth rather than validity of activation data.

Significant disagreement on chemokine-receptor interactions (C6, C71-C80). OpenEval finds computational predictions supported but requiring validation. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 3 specifically noting 'signal mechanism was not evaluated,' indicating lack of functional validation. Both acknowledge these are computational predictions.

Agreement on myeloid cell characterization (C60-C65, C68, C69). Both evaluations support the neutrophil infiltration and activation findings from scRNA-seq data. OpenEval notes some inferences are speculative while peer review implicitly accepts the characterization.

Complete agreement on osteoclastogenic factor expression (C82-C91). Both evaluations support the M-CSF and RANKL data, with OpenEval noting C91 (AG fibroblast-derived factors inducing osteoclastic activity) is somewhat speculative, while peer review accepts findings as part of overall AG fibroblast characterization.

Agreement on ILC3 identification as IL-17 producers (C8, C92-C97, C141, C143). Both evaluations support this finding as a significant discovery, with peer review specifically acknowledging ILC findings as part of the study's contributions.

Complete agreement on ILC3 involvement in bone resorption (C9, C102, C103, C105-C107, C151, C152, C155). Both evaluations support the knockout mouse experiments demonstrating ILC3 role, with peer review accepting the proposed AG fibroblast-neutrophil-ILC3 axis.

Agreement on IL-6 temporal shift and ILC3 support (C7, C110-C112, C115-C118, C157-C160). OpenEval finds data supported but notes inferences about ILC3 induction and collective environment are speculative. Peer review supports the IL-6/IL-23a patterns as part of accepted mechanistic framework.

Partial overlap on ILC3 interactions (C117, C118, C120, C159, C160). OpenEval finds temporal shift supported but collective environment inference speculative. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, noting 'signal mechanism was not evaluated' and these remain inferential rather than mechanistically validated.

Perfect agreement on periodontitis model characterization (C22-C27). Both evaluations support the temporal progression documentation and model validation, with peer review noting general limitation about mouse vs human models rather than critiquing characterization itself.

OpenEval evaluates NicheNet computational analysis (C120-C123) as supported but requiring validation. Peer review groups C120 with other ILC3 interaction claims and rates as UNCERTAIN due to lack of mechanistic evaluation.

Disagreement on main conclusions (C124-C126, C161). OpenEval finds conclusions well-supported by collective data though direct causation is inferred. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, stating 'results partially support their conclusions' and noting signal mechanisms were not evaluated, indicating mechanistic model lacks full validation.

OpenEval groups speculative interpretations (C38, C41, C44, C58, C70, C91, C133, C134, C138, C160, C162-C165) as UNCERTAIN, noting they require additional validation. Peer review overlaps on C134, C162 and similarly rates mechanistic conclusions as UNCERTAIN due to lack of functional demonstration.
OpenEval includes C138 (chemokine interactions) in speculative claims rated UNCERTAIN. Peer review also rates chemokine-receptor interactions as UNCERTAIN, both noting lack of functional validation.

OpenEval evaluates epithelial cell heterogeneity and IL-6 expression (C113, C114) as supported, providing context for IL-6 sources. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims.

OpenEval evaluates extensive background claims (C1, C10-C21, C59, C66, C81, C98, C109, C127-C130, C135, C137, C139, C140, C142, C144-C150, C153, C154, C156) as supported by prior literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found as reviewers did not separately assess background statements.
OpenEval evaluates claims about previous work (C45-C47) as appropriately cited. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these methodological justification claims.
OpenEval evaluates translational relevance to human clinical patterns (C108) as supported by comparative images. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific translational claim.

OpenEval evaluates fibroblast heterogeneity refinement (C131, C132) as supported. Peer review includes C132 in overall mechanistic conclusions rated as UNCERTAIN, though the descriptive finding of heterogeneity itself is not questioned.
